transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

That musty smell is almost always caused by a build-up of bacteria and detergent residue in the door seal folds, the detergent drawer or the pump filter. It’s not usually a broken part. Here is what to do:
1. Unplug the machine for safety.
2. Pull back the rubber door seal (the bellows) and wipe out any black mould or slime from inside the folds with an old towel or cloth.
3. Remove the detergent drawer and wash it thoroughly in hot soapy water, checking for gunk at the bottom of the slot where it slides in.
4. Locate the pump filter (usually behind a small panel at the bottom front). Place towels underneath, unscrew it slowly to let any water out, and clean it completely.
5. Run an empty wash cycle at 90°C using a washing machine cleaner or two tablespoons of soda crystals. After that, always leave the door and drawer slightly ajar between uses so air can circulate and dry everything out. If the smell persists after this deep clean, let me know.
ok thanks, will have a go. do i need to do the 90 wash with nothing in it? also theres a drum clean light that comes on sometimes, no idea what that means

Yes, you need to run that 90°C cycle with nothing in it. That high temperature is what kills the bacteria and dissolves the detergent scum that causes the musty smell. Regarding the drum clean light: on Samsung machines this usually means the machine has detected a certain number of washes (often around 30) and is reminding you to run a maintenance cycle. It’s not an error code, just a timer reset reminder.
